intro: Biggest rank disagreements between the SEI board and SP+, 2026 season: from the SP+ top 15 and from our own top 15.

teams.explanation: SP+ bought the resume: 6-2 with a +100 margin and Big 12 wins like 34-7 over Cincinnati, 39-3 over Iowa State and 52-31 at West Virginia. Our play data didn't. Arizona's offense turns the ball over (INT% z-1.12) and draws flags (penalty z-1.30) with no push up front (line play z-0.59); the defense generates nothing takeaways-wise (INT% z-1.08). Road losses at BYU (17-28) and Texas Tech (26-34) filled in exactly what the metrics forecast. The scoreboard outran the process.
hints: Scoreboard outran process: margin rank #19 (margin +100) but SEI #56.

teams.explanation: Our board loves how Kentucky plays: opponent INT% z+2.41, turnover generation z+1.92, ball security z+1.21 (off INT% z+2.04) and early-down rush PPA z+1.52. SP+ sees the scoreboard: 7-1 on a +33 margin that ranks #47, with field-goal wins at South Carolina (35-34) and over LSU (35-34). SP+'s own halves (off #40, def #53) agree the underlying play is ordinary. The 17-45 home loss to Alabama is why the resume doesn't move SP+ either. The play data is what lifts Kentucky to #13.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #47 (margin +33) but SEI #13.
Strongest metrics: INT% +2.41, INT% +2.04, Early rush PPA +1.52.

teams.explanation: SP+ loves the results — #9 overall, offense #8. Our offense metrics disagree: early-down pass PPA z-0.71, INT% z-0.64, SEI off #46. What's genuinely strong is the defense: INT% z+2.85, third-down pass PPA z+1.56, SEI def #18. The 34-26 win over Arizona and 53-25 over Arizona State are resume wins SP+ credits; the 24-37 loss at Cincinnati and a 28-26 squeaker vs Houston show how fragile the offense is. Tech's gap is an SEI offense grade SP+ simply doesn't share.
hints: Offense drives the gap: SEI off #46 vs def #18.

teams.explanation: The margin does most of the talking: +170, built on 57-3 over Stanford, 51-7 over Virginia and 41-7 at Cal. Our board reads that as real process — defensive explosiveness allowed z+3.04 (nobody breaks a play on Wake) and offensive INT% z+1.64. SP+'s halves (off #20, def #33) don't follow, and one-score road wins at Purdue (38-36) and Louisville (30-27), plus a 20-33 home loss to Miami, cap SP+'s respect. Wake's blowouts and our z-scores agree with each other; SP+ sits between them.

The offense is the whole gap: third-down pass PPA z-1.62, explosiveness z-0.83, an SEI offense ranked #71. The defense carries the scoreboard — sack% z+2.40, opponent red-zone TD% z+1.54, SEI def #6 — good enough to hang a 26-10 on Alabama. But close games flag the passing stagnation: 17-20 to Texas, 24-27 at South Carolina, 24-17 at Arkansas, three of seven FBS games by one score. SP+ averages the results to #11; our metrics call it a top-10 defense dragging a bottom-third offense.
hints: Offense drives the gap: SEI off #71 vs def #6.
3 of 7 games decided by <=7 pts (SP+ penalizes close wins harder than SEI does).

teams.explanation: An offense that outplays its record: explosive-play rate z+3.05, third-down rush PPA z+3.06 — SP+ itself puts the attack at #5. What SP+ can't forgive is the defense (#65 in their halves) and three losses by exactly three points: 38-41 at Ole Miss, 27-30 to Wake, 28-31 at NC State. Our margin (+61, #32) lags the play because of those three games. SEI weights the process — 52-24 over Stanford and 44-20 over Florida State are what the metrics want — and forgives outcomes the win column doesn't.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #32 (margin +61) but SEI #14.
Defense drives the gap: SEI off #11 vs def #38.
Strongest metrics: 3rd rush PPA +3.06, Exp +3.05, 3rd rush PPA +2.34.
3 of 6 games decided by <=7 pts (SP+ penalizes close wins harder than SEI does).

teams.explanation: Eight wins and +132 — the country's tenth-best margin — is what pulls SP+ to #10. Our metrics don't track the scoreboard: run-game stuff rate against them z-2.06, INT% z-1.44, and two merely average halves (SEI off #24, def #31). Wins like 27-24 at Colorado and 41-24 over Kansas produce results without dominant play; the 49-25 rout at Cincinnati and 31-17 at Iowa State keep the resume respectable. SP+ buys the win-based profile. Our z-scores say the margin is better than the team.
hints: Scoreboard outran process: margin rank #10 (margin +132) but SEI #20.

teams.explanation: Eight wins ride on the defense — our #3 unit, with turnover generation z+2.23: Havoc z+2.25, INT% z+2.25, fumble-forcing rate z+2.21. The offense (#44) leans on early-down rushing (z+2.34) and undermines itself with ball security (fum% z-1.57). The grind games — 17-15 at Oregon, 17-7 over Wisconsin — are why SP+ sits at #17; the 54-3 rout at Maryland and 52-38 over Purdue are why we sit at #8. SP+'s halves (off #38, def #21) undervalue how thoroughly UCLA takes the ball.
hints: Offense drives the gap: SEI off #44 vs def #3.
Strongest metrics: Early rush PPA +2.34, Havoc +2.25, INT% +2.25.

teams.explanation: SEI likes how Nebraska actually plays: red-zone TD% z+2.16 and third-down pass PPA z+1.75 on offense, z+2.21 on passing downs plus INT% z+1.68 at the other end. SP+'s #15 tracks the results slide — 17-20 to Indiana, 14-17 at Oregon, 10-17 to Washington, three straight one-score losses a win-based model can't shrug off. The 31-13 win at Michigan State and 48-23 over Maryland are why our rating stays near the top ten. Penalties (z-1.59) are the one real flaw.
hints: Strongest metrics: 3rd pass PPA +2.21, RZ TD% +2.16, 3rd pass PPA +1.75.
